blocker: Sizing concern (not a build blocker, attribute kept verbatim per HARD RULE): the original hashbench declared heap_size=33554432, stack_size=10485760, max_trace_length=50000000, but the frozen template attribute is heap_size=32768/max_trace_length=65536. The full benchmark (four hash families over sizes up to 2049B) generates far more than 65536 trace cycles, so emulation may hit the trace-length ceiling identically on both arms; this is a harness-sizing limitation, not a portability defect, and cannot be changed without editing the frozen attribute.
decode_layout: No input consumed. Original hashbench() takes zero arguments and derives all inputs from fixed internal seeds; `input: Vec<u8>` is intentionally ignored, so DECODE is total for any input length (including empty). Output ENCODE: the lifted body's [u8;32] return value (always all-zero) emitted as 32 output bytes. Divergence surfaces via assert_eq panics inside the verify_all! checks (or instrumentation), not via output bytes.
entry_called: hashbench_body() — the verbatim lifted body of the original #[jolt::provable] fn hashbench(), calling bench_sha256/bench_keccak/bench_blake2b/bench_blake3/bench_blake3_keyed64
